strategies.summary: Mark the bullish order blocks formed during the sell curve into a higher-timeframe discount array. After price shifts into the buy curve and reclaims one from below, only trade the retest when a new right-curve PD array overlaps that block.

timeframes.notes: The transcript explicitly uses 4h context and 15m execution. The higher-timeframe array lives on bias_tf; the order block, reclaim, overlap, and entry all run on 15m.

glossary.Market maker model: A sell curve into a higher-timeframe discount array followed by a buy curve; here proxied by custom_signals.market_maker_curve_shift.
glossary.Reclaimed order block: A bullish order block from the sell curve that price later closes back above on the buy curve; see custom_signals.reclaimed_trade_through.

custom_signals.name: htf_pd_array_tap
custom_signals.plain_definition: Price trades into a higher-timeframe discount array (bullish) or premium array (bearish), such as a fair value gap or order block.
custom_signals.numeric_definition: (low <= bullish_fvg[0].gap_high@bias_tf AND high >= bullish_fvg[0].gap_low@bias_tf AND NOT bullish_fvg[0].filled@bias_tf) OR (low <= bullish_ob[0].zone_high@bias_tf AND high >= bullish_ob[0].zone_low@bias_tf AND NOT bullish_ob[0].invalidated@bias_tf)

custom_signals.name: market_maker_curve_shift
custom_signals.plain_definition: Price taps a higher-timeframe discount array and then prints a bullish structure shift on the setup timeframe, starting the buy curve of the market maker model.
custom_signals.numeric_definition: custom_signals.htf_pd_array_tap AND (structural_event.kind == bullish_choch OR structural_event.kind == bullish_bos)

custom_signals.name: reclaimed_trade_through
custom_signals.plain_definition: Price closes back above the high of the left-curve bullish order block, reclaiming it as support on the buy curve.

custom_signals.name: breaker_pattern
custom_signals.plain_definition: A high forms, price then sweeps the prior swing low, and then closes back above that high; the up candle(s) at the broken high form the breaker block.
custom_signals.numeric_definition: swing_low[0].price < swing_low[1].price AND swing_high[0].open_time > swing_low[1].open_time AND swing_high[0].open_time < swing_low[0].open_time AND close > swing_high[0].price AND close[-1] <= swing_high[0].price

custom_signals.name: swing_failure_pattern
custom_signals.plain_definition: A low, a high, a higher low (the low is not swept), then a close above that high; the broken high is the mitigation block.
custom_signals.numeric_definition: swing_low[0].price > swing_low[1].price AND swing_high[0].open_time > swing_low[1].open_time AND swing_high[0].open_time < swing_low[0].open_time AND close > swing_high[0].price AND close[-1] <= swing_high[0].price

custom_signals.name: reclaimed_pd_array_overlap
custom_signals.plain_definition: The reclaimed bullish order block overlaps a newly formed right-curve PD array: a bullish fair value gap, a later bullish order block, a breaker pattern level, or a swing-failure-pattern mitigation level.
custom_signals.numeric_definition: (bullish_fvg[0].confirmed_at > order_block.anchor_at AND max(order_block.zone_low, bullish_fvg[0].gap_low) <= min(order_block.zone_high, bullish_fvg[0].gap_high) AND NOT bullish_fvg[0].filled) OR (bullish_ob[0].anchor_at > order_block.anchor_at AND max(order_block.zone_low, bullish_ob[0].zone_low) <= min(order_block.zone_high, bullish_ob[0].zone_high) AND NOT bullish_ob[0].invalidated) OR (custom_signals.breaker_pattern >= order_block.zone_low AND custom_signals.breaker_pattern <= order_block.zone_high) OR (custom_signals.swing_failure_pattern >= order_block.zone_low AND custom_signals.swing_failure_pattern <= order_block.zone_high)

sequence: Mark the bullish order block formed during the sell curve into the higher-timeframe discount array.
Wait for the higher-timeframe array tap and bullish structure shift that starts the buy curve.
Wait for price to close back above that left-curve bullish order block so it becomes reclaimed support.
Only keep the setup if a new right-curve PD array overlaps the reclaimed block, then buy the retest of that reclaimed block.

filters.text: Never trade a reclaimed order block in isolation. It MUST overlap with another PD array to avoid chart clutter and low-probability random bounces.

entry_rule.text: Buy the retracement into the reclaimed bullish order block once a new right-curve PD array overlaps it.
entry_rule.quote: where does it go higher off of is fair value gap overlapping with the other two discount arrays

presenter_claims.claim: if you have a thousand PD arrays on your chart then you are not accurate No you're just guessing
that's exactly what makes PD arrays so strong when they are overlapping with another PD array

strategies.notes: Written on the canonical bullish side; the bearish examples are the mirror. The market maker model is proxied as a 4h array tap plus a bullish CHoCH/BOS on 15m, because the presenter names the curve logic but does not define a separate detector for the full two-curve profile. The overlap filter keeps right-curve confluence with a new FVG, a later order block, a breaker level, or a swing-failure-pattern mitigation level.

setup_walkthrough.what_happens: Price moves down forming a sell curve towards a HTF discount array. During this leg, institutions buy and form regular bullish order blocks.
Price hits the discount array, shifts market structure, and begins the upward buy curve.
Price trades above the old bullish order blocks from the sell curve, officially turning them into reclaimed order blocks that now act as support.

examples.presenter_commentary: The presenter explains the fundamental logic of a market maker model: institutions accumulate long positions during the sell curve, forming order blocks. Once the trend shifts to the buy curve, these same blocks become reclaimed and provide support.

Price retraces into this triple-confluence discount array zone and bounces higher.
